device.name: PrusaLink (Prusa MK4 / MK3.9 / XL / Mini)
device.notes:
PrusaLink is Prusa's on-printer web server (MK4, MK3.9, XL, Mini) with a published OpenAPI spec. Local HTTP on the printer's LAN IP, no cloud. AUTH is HTTP Digest (username `maker` + the printer's password/PIN) and/or an X-Api-Key header. A legacy OctoPrint-compatible /api/ surface exists for older clients.
ENDPOINTS:
  GET  /api/version                    API + firmware version
  GET  /api/v1/info                     device info
  GET  /api/v1/status                   real-time printer/job/transfer/storage/
                                        camera telemetry
  GET  /api/v1/job                      current job
  PUT  /api/v1/job/{id}/pause | /resume | /continue
  DELETE /api/v1/job/{id}               stop
  PUT  /api/v1/files/{storage}/{path}   upload G-code
  POST /api/v1/files/{storage}/{path}   start a print of an uploaded file
  HEAD /api/v1/files/{storage}/{path}   check presence
  DELETE /api/v1/files/{storage}/{path} remove

openness.notes: Vendor-provided and documented (open OpenAPI spec; the firmware itself is GPL). Upstream is authoritative.

upstream_docs.covers: The /api/v1 endpoints, the auth (Digest maker + X-Api-Key), and the OctoPrint-compatible layer.
upstream_docs.title: PrusaLink — OpenAPI spec

enter_pairing_mode.notes: A persistent setting rather than a timed window: once on, PrusaLink answers whenever the printer is on the network.

procedures.basis: Prusa's Wi-Fi and PrusaLink setup guide (help.prusa3d.com) for the MK4/MK3.9/XL/MINI, which gives the Settings > Network > PrusaLink path, and the PrusaLink OpenAPI spec's digest security scheme.
procedures.name: Enable PrusaLink and read the credentials from the printer menu

steps.action: On the printer's LCD, open Settings > Network > PrusaLink and switch PrusaLink on.
Note the username (maker), the password and the printer's IP from that screen.
Call GET /api/v1/status with HTTP Digest (maker + password) or an X-Api-Key header.
steps.expect: 200 with printer telemetry; 401 means a wrong or stale credential.

exclusivity.recovery: A 401 after a firmware update or reset means the password changed: read it off the printer again. PrusaSlicer users moving between Digest and API-key authentication see the same 401 and fix it by selecting the matching method in the slicer's physical-printer settings.

pairing.notes: The gate is a per-printer password the printer makes up itself and shows on its own screen; the username is always `maker`. Possession of that pair is the whole of local authorisation, over HTTP Digest (or the same value as X-Api-Key), and it involves no Prusa account — Prusa Connect, the vendor cloud, is a separate opt-in and its death costs PrusaLink nothing. See setup method `device_ui` and `credentials.issued_to_client`.

pin.notes: The PrusaLink password, generated by the printer and shown on its own display under Settings > Network > PrusaLink, alongside the fixed username `maker`. Per-unit, so no value appears here. On current firmware the same string also serves as the X-Api-Key value; older builds offered only the API key. Every client presents the same credential — nothing per-client is issued.

unpair.notes: There are no per-client credentials to revoke. Owners report being able to have the printer generate a new password, which would lock out every client at once, but the menu entry was not confirmed here; a factory reset is known to reissue it (see setup.factory_reset). There is no way to set your own username or password on the printer.

issued_to_client: API key / maker password (read from the printer screen)
credentials.notes: Local control uses the printer's API key / maker password over HTTP Digest. Onboarding is via the printer UI, not this API.

factory_reset.description: Menu-driven rather than a button hold. Note that the button under the rotary knob is NOT this: it is a reset in the reboot sense — the vendor documents it as equivalent to switching the printer off and on — and someone reaching for a factory reset will find it first.
factory_reset.effect: Resets every saved value on the printer to its default state. Expect the network configuration and the PrusaLink API key to go with it, so any client holding that key must be given the new one.

procedures.basis: Prusa's MK4/MK3.9 handbook and MK4S user manual, section 4.13 Factory Reset.
procedures.name: Factory Reset from the printer's own menu

steps.action: On the printer's LCD, open Settings, then System, then Factory Reset.
steps.expect: All saved values return to their default state.

methods.description: Enable PrusaLink in the printer network settings, note the IP and API key/password from the screen, then call /api/v1 over HTTP Digest (maker + password) or with the X-Api-Key header.

steps.action: Enable PrusaLink in the printer network settings; read the IP and API key/password.
Call GET /api/v1/status (Digest maker + password, or X-Api-Key).

setup.notes: Enable PrusaLink in the printer's network settings; the screen shows the API key/password and IP. Connect with `maker` + password (Digest) or the API key header. No cloud.

rejoin.notes: Network settings are changed from the printer menu while reachable.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The endpoints and auth are from Prusa's own PrusaLink OpenAPI spec.
